minutes.headline: School Committee approved a 10-member superintendent screening committee 5-0 despite members' reservations about its diversity of viewpoints
minutes.summary: In a short special meeting, the School Committee reviewed and voted on the superintendent screening subcommittee's recommended 10-person list (from 20 applicants) to serve on the search's screening committee. Several members voiced reservations that the list skewed toward current employees and parents and lacked athletics representation or dissenting community voices, but no changes were made and the list passed unanimously by roll call; the committee also agreed to hold public listening sessions on desired superintendent qualities.

what_happened.line: School Committee voted 5-0 to approve a 10-member superintendent screening committee as recommended, without changes.
Before the vote, several members said the recommended list leaned toward current employees and parents and lacked athletics or dissenting community voices.
The subcommittee reported no additional applicants had come in by the January 31 deadline, so the original list went forward unchanged.
The committee agreed to hold public listening sessions for residents to weigh in on what qualities the next superintendent should have.
The chair said she would contact applicants who were not chosen to keep them engaged in the search process.

why_it_matters: This committee will screen candidates for superintendent, a hire that shapes district leadership and, ultimately, budget and program decisions for years.
Members' own concerns about who is and isn't represented on the screening committee may affect whose priorities get weight early in the search.
The planned listening sessions are a specific opportunity for residents to influence the criteria used to pick the next superintendent.
